recap:
## Decisions
- Drop the full intelligent controller (speech and gesture recognition). Merge the "Google" (easy to use, sophisticated) and "fancy" concepts into one controller. [00:27:02]
- Power the remote with both solar energy and regular batteries. [00:27:06]
- Use low-level (cheap) chips. [00:20:13]
- Use wood for the case. [00:27:06]
- Use lighted LCD buttons. [00:27:23]
- Add simple vocal commands as an added value, such as switching channels and turning the TV on or off. [00:28:41]

## Action items
- ID, UI, ME: Work on the look-and-feel design for an easy-to-use, powerful, fancy remote with simple vocal command recognition. [00:29:03]
- owner not assigned: Find a nice shape for the wooden remote control. [00:29:30]
- owner not assigned: Take the fruits-and-vegetables fashion trend into account in the design. [00:29:42]
- ID, UI: Build the prototype together and show a clay model at the next meeting. [00:30:13]

## Unresolved
- Wood may not fit users' wish for a spongy touch. ME suggested wood with rubber buttons, and ID suggested wood only on the bottom, but neither was settled. [00:25:57]
- Voice recognition may need adapting for each country's language. Its cost against the 12-euro price target was not settled. [00:08:35]
- ID asked whether voice control belongs in the TV rather than the remote. ID also suggested a marketing study on user interest in voice, but no one took it on. [00:26:40]
- ME asked about a touch screen, and nobody answered. [00:20:52]
